back: A large body of air with similar temperature and humidity across it, acquired in a source region.
c = continental (dry), m = maritime (moist); E equatorial, T tropical, P polar. So cT is hot and dry; mT is warm and moist; cP is cold and dry.
Heating from below makes air unstable (showers); cooling from below makes it stable (fog, stratus); crossing seas adds moisture; crossing mountains removes it.
Low pressure system: air converges and rises; cloud, rain and strong winds. Southern hemisphere circulation is clockwise.
High pressure system: air descends and spreads out; clear, dry, light winds. Southern hemisphere circulation is anticlockwise.
Pressure difference (hPa) ÷ distance (km) × 100 = hPa per 100 km. Steeper gradient means stronger wind.
Heavy rain or showers as it passes; then temperature falls sharply, pressure rises and the sky clears.
Cool, misty drizzle on the Zimbabwean plateau, caused by moist Indian Ocean air lifted and cooled.
Tropical maritime (Indian Ocean), equatorial/Congo air (summer rain), tropical continental (hot dry), cold dry air behind fronts (cool season).
